note: Every entry was checked against the code at the listed file and line. Starlink is drawn on the globe for connectivity context; it is not a data source.

sources.name: Sentinel-2 L2A surface reflectance
sources.provider: ESA Copernicus, served from the AWS Open Data registry
sources.used_for: Every pass over the farms: NDVI and NBR per field, the harvest curve, burn scars, flood and stress cues, the time-lapse frames.
sources.why: The one free satellite that sees every field at 10 m every few days; the whole season is read from it.
sources.cadence: every 2 to 5 days per field (clouds permitting)
sources.licence: Copernicus Sentinel data: free, full and open
sources.live_or_offline: fetched by the pipeline and cached

sources.name: Earth Search STAC catalog
sources.used_for: Finding every Sentinel-2 scene over the landscape by date and cloud cover.
sources.why: A free catalog that lets the pipeline ask for scenes instead of crawling buckets.
sources.licence: Free STAC API over open data (Element 84 terms)

sources.name: Esri World Imagery
sources.used_for: The sub-metre aerial basemap under the farm map; what shows when you zoom past what Sentinel-2 can resolve.
sources.why: Sentinel-2 is 10 m per pixel; past zoom 15 a farmer needs to see their own buildings and lanes.
sources.cadence: updated by Esri over months to years
sources.licence: Esri ArcGIS Online terms of use; attribution required

sources.name: Open-Meteo forecast
sources.used_for: The 14-day daily forecast: rain, minimum and maximum temperature, that every plan reads.
sources.why: Free, no key, global, with the same fields everywhere Overfield might run.
sources.cadence: hourly runs; the plan reads the morning run
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Open-Meteo); free API for non-commercial use

sources.name: Open-Meteo previous runs
sources.used_for: The forecast as it was issued on an earlier morning, so a replay judges the plan with what was known then, not hindsight.
sources.why: A warning only counts if it was possible on the day; the archive of issued forecasts proves it.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Open-Meteo); free API for non-commercial use

sources.name: Open-Meteo multi-model ensemble
sources.used_for: Eight weather models read side by side; the plan says how many agree on heavy rain or frost.
sources.why: One model can be wrong about one storm; agreement across eight is what a farmer can act on.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Open-Meteo); free API for non-commercial use

sources.name: ECMWF IFS 0.25 degree
sources.used_for: Ensemble member.
sources.why: The global reference model.
sources.licence: ECMWF open data, CC BY 4.0

sources.name: NOAA GFS and HRRR
sources.used_for: Ensemble member (HRRR for the first 48 h over the US).
sources.why: The US model with the finest short-range detail.
sources.licence: US government work, public domain

sources.name: DWD ICON
sources.used_for: Ensemble member.
sources.why: An independent global model from a second agency.
sources.licence: DWD open data (German open data licence)

sources.name: Canadian GEM
sources.used_for: Ensemble member.
sources.why: A third agency's global model.
sources.licence: Environment and Climate Change Canada data licence

sources.name: Meteo-France ARPEGE and AROME
sources.used_for: Ensemble member.
sources.why: A fourth agency's global model.
sources.licence: Meteo-France open data (Etalab)

sources.name: UK Met Office global
sources.used_for: Ensemble member.
sources.why: A fifth agency's global model.
sources.licence: UK Met Office data under CC BY-SA 4.0

sources.name: JMA GSM and MSM
sources.used_for: Ensemble member.
sources.why: A sixth agency's global model.
sources.licence: JMA open data

sources.name: NOAA National Blend of Models
sources.used_for: Ensemble member (CONUS).
sources.why: The forecasters' own blend for the US.
sources.licence: US government work, public domain

sources.name: NASA POWER daily
sources.used_for: Daily temperature and rain per county for every training year of the yield model.
sources.why: The yield model needs the same weather history for 99 counties over 7 years; POWER gives it without a key.
sources.licence: NASA open data, no restrictions

sources.name: SoilGrids 2.0
sources.used_for: Organic carbon, clay, sand and pH at 0 to 30 cm for every field; the texture class in the yield notes.
sources.why: Soil explains why two neighbouring fields yield differently under the same sky.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0
sources.live_or_offline: fetched once per field and cached

sources.name: Open-Meteo elevation (Copernicus DEM GLO-90)
sources.used_for: Elevation and a 100 m slope stencil per field; aspect in the yield notes.
sources.why: Slope and aspect change how fast a field drains and dries.
sources.licence: Copernicus DEM: free and open; API CC BY 4.0
sources.live_or_offline: fetched once per field and cached

sources.name: USDA NASS QuickStats county yields
sources.used_for: Measured county corn and soybean yields for all 99 Iowa counties, 2008 to 2025: the training set of the county yield model (yield_train.py).
sources.why: The ground truth for yield in the US, public domain; eighteen seasons lift the held-out R² to 0.62 for corn and 0.71 for soybeans.
sources.licence: US government work, public domain; free API key
sources.live_or_offline: fetched with NASS_API_KEY and cached; the committed yield_model.json was trained on it

sources.name: CropNet USDA crop dataset
sources.used_for: The same USDA county yield tables for 2016 to 2022, the fallback training set when no NASS key is set; the committed model no longer uses it.
sources.why: A ready-made, cleaned table of USDA county yields that lets the model train with no key at all.
sources.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0, research use only
sources.live_or_offline: downloaded once and cached; fallback only

sources.name: US Census Bureau county gazetteer 2023
sources.used_for: County centroids that place each county's weather history.
sources.why: The yield model needs one point per county for NASA POWER.
sources.licence: US government work, public domain

sources.name: Fields of The World
sources.used_for: Open global field boundaries, drawn on the yield map for comparison with the roster's farms.
sources.why: Shows how the farms would be found anywhere on Earth without a hand-drawn roster.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0
sources.live_or_offline: extracted once from the Iowa parquet (145 polygons in the demo box) and committed as data/out/ftw_fields_2024.geojson; a display overlay, not an input to any plan

sources.name: NASA FIRMS VIIRS active fires
sources.used_for: Near-real-time hotspots that confirm a burn scar or raise the fire check.
sources.why: A dark patch in imagery is only a fire if something was burning; FIRMS says whether it was.
sources.licence: NASA open data; free MAP_KEY

sources.name: OpenStreetMap Nominatim
sources.used_for: Turns a farm address into a point at sign-up so the right field is matched.
sources.why: Free, global, no key; one request per sign-up.
sources.licence: OpenStreetMap data under ODbL; Nominatim usage policy (light use, identify yourself)

sources.name: Perceptron Mk1.5 vision model
sources.used_for: Reads the true-colour frames for standing crop, change between passes, flood and stress cues (insights.json).
sources.why: A second, independent reading of the imagery to cross-check the index curves.
sources.licence: Paid API (per-token pricing); key required

sources.name: Photon 2.0 SMS and iMessage
sources.used_for: The morning text to every farmer and the officer, and the inbound questions.
sources.why: Farmers read texts; no app to install.
sources.licence: Photon terms of service; key required
sources.live_or_offline: live from the morning queue only

sources.name: Twilio Programmable Voice
sources.used_for: Places the morning call and bridges the voice session.
sources.why: A phone call reaches people who do not read texts, in their language.
sources.licence: Twilio terms of service; key required
sources.live_or_offline: live from the morning queue only

sources.name: Grok Voice realtime
sources.used_for: The voice on the call: reads the plan and answers questions about that farm only.
sources.why: A natural voice in the farmer's language with the plan as its only facts.
sources.licence: xAI terms; key required

sources.name: Grok chat
sources.used_for: Translation of the plan words and the officer's questions over the finished files.
sources.why: Never invents a measurement: it only rewords facts from plans.json and route.json.
sources.licence: xAI terms; key required

sources.name: Email (SMTP)
sources.used_for: The optional third channel for the morning plan.
sources.why: Some people asked for email at sign-up.
sources.licence: The mailbox provider's terms
sources.live_or_offline: live from the morning queue only

sources.name: USDA NASS Crop Progress
sources.used_for: Weekly percent harvested for central Iowa, used to check the satellite harvest curve against the official survey.
sources.why: The satellite harvest model is only trusted because it can be scored against the official weekly numbers.
sources.licence: US government work, public domain; free API key
sources.live_or_offline: code in place (validate_usda.py --refresh); the published run scored against the built-in sample rows, the real fetch needs NASS_API_KEY

sources.name: CelesTrak orbital elements
sources.used_for: Orbital elements for Sentinel-2A/B/C, Landsat 8/9, Terra, Aqua and the Starlink shell on the globe, propagated with SGP4.
sources.why: The satellites on the globe are real: their positions come from the same elements trackers use.
sources.licence: Free for any use with attribution (CelesTrak)
sources.live_or_offline: snapshot in the repo; propagated in the browser

sources.name: three.js Earth textures
sources.used_for: The day, night-lights, normal and specular maps on the globe.
sources.why: Public-domain NASA imagery packaged for the renderer.
sources.licence: MIT (three.js); NASA imagery public domain

sources.name: GitHub Pages
sources.used_for: Hosts the site and the published plan files that the developer API serves.
sources.why: Free static hosting straight from the repository.
sources.licence: GitHub terms of service

sources.name: Supabase
sources.used_for: Accounts, farm profiles, developer keys, terms acceptances and the delivery log, behind row-level security.
sources.why: Sign-in and a database without running a server.
sources.licence: Supabase terms of service; keys required
